doc.title: Pete Candoli interviewed by Monk Rowe, Los Angeles, California, February 15, 1999

title: Alcohol, drugs and Jimmy Rowles
summary: Pete speaks about dissipation among musicians and his friend Jimmy Rowles.

story.theme_name: Drink, drugs and the bandstand's casualties
story.community_name: Drugs and drink on the bandstand and the road

blocks.x: You remained pretty healthy. Not so with some of the musicians.

You know there was a time when dissipation was the thing, unfortunately, you know the drug scene or getting strung out. Well it’s like when people used to booze, you know, liked to take drinks. Later on, I’m talking about 45, 50 years ago, nobody thought anything about drinking. But then they found out about this thing called alcoholism, you know, and then later, Alcoholics Anonymous and things like that, because it’s a real sickness in a sense. You know if it’s in the genes prior, that it can be very — and I used to know guys that used to have a few drinks before they can play. And that’s too bad because I don’t know why, nice guys, nice as you are. One of my closest friends, Jimmy Rowles, was an alcoholic and we traveled with Peggy and finally the doctor says hey, “I don’t want to be your doctor, I don’t want to be responsible.” And God bless him, such a beautiful guy, and such a monster musically speaking. Other people like that, friends, I go on talking about them, I mean wonderful people, wonderful guys. And they gave me so much inspiration and really I’ve been a very lucky guy.
